speaker: Buck
teaser: Forty years of duck hunting. Now the ducks sneak up on him.
hello: Buck Shotwell. Forty years in a duck blind, every frosty dawn I could get.
Nowadays the ducks sneak up on me. And the wife says my left ear's gone on strike.

which_ear.say: The left, no contest. The phone lives on my right ear these days.
which_ear.note: Worse on the left; phone lives on the right

onset.say: Slow. Crept up over the years, like fog on the marsh. Nothing sudden.

ringing.say: A high whine in both ears. Louder on the left. Like a mosquito that never lands.
ringing.note: Whine in both ears, louder on the left

red_flags.say: No pain, no leaking, no spinning. Steady as a wooden decoy.

say: Forty years of duck hunting. Twelve-gauge on my right shoulder.
Earplugs? Never. Figured I'd miss the ducks talking.
noise.note: 40 years of shotguns, right-handed, no plugs

ear_history.say: Never had an ear infection. No operations, never took a knock to the head.

family.say: My dad got a bit deaf. Mind you, he ran a sawmill for thirty years.
family.note: Dad had some loss; he ran a sawmill

health.say: Fit as a fiddle. One little pill for cholesterol. That's the lot.

aids.say: Never. The wife's been on at me for years. My retriever doesn't nag.

say: In the truck, the wife's on my left. Half of what she says blows out the window.
At dawn I can't hear the wings whistle any more. The ducks are on me before I see 'em.
And the lodge meetings. Whoever sits on my left might as well be miming.
hardest.note: Trouble: wife in the truck, duck wings, lodge

right.caption: Buck's RIGHT ear: a clean canal and a pearly, healthy eardrum. Not a feather in sight.

left.caption: Buck's LEFT ear: just as clean and healthy. It looks exactly like the right one.

decision_lines.fit: Fit! Shooting explains the left ear, and no other red flags. Aids, plugs, and a yearly recheck.
decision_lines.refer: Many clinics would refer this. Here, shooting likely explains it, nothing else flags: fit, recheck yearly.
decision_lines.today: Nothing sudden: it crept in over forty seasons. No emergency, and no other red flags.
decision_lines.clear: No aids? His left ear sits near 60 dB up high. The right is slipping too.

why.prompt: Why can Buck be fitted without seeing a doctor first?
options: Shooting explains why his left ear is worse.
Right! A right-hander's left ear sits nearer the muzzle. A likely cause, and no other red flags.
A lopsided loss never needs a doctor.
It does when nothing explains it, or it came on fast. Buck's shooting explains his.
Ringing in both ears rules out a problem.
Ringing rules nothing out. Both-ear ringing is common with noise; one-sided ringing is a flag.
His tympanograms were both type A.
Type A says the eardrums move well. It can't explain why one ear is worse.

debrief: His pattern points to the shotgun: the ear nearer the muzzle takes the blast. For right-handers, the left.
One ear worse is a red flag, unless something explains it. Buck's shotgun does; nothing else flags.
The truck and the lodge are goals for the aids. The duck wings? That's the electronic muffs' job.
Recheck him every year. If the left keeps slipping away from the right, then a doctor.
goodbye: Hold on. Is that a sparrow outside? Haven't heard one of those in years.
The damage so far stays, but more is preventable. Earplugs AND earmuffs, every shot.
Plugs? Then how do I hear the ducks coming?
Plugs under electronic muffs. The muffs turn soft sounds up and shut out the bang.
Back in two weeks to check the truck and the lodge. Then a hearing test every year.
Plugs under muffs, two weeks, every year. Sold. See you then, owl.

headlines.S: BUCK FITTED; DUCKS CAN'T SNEAK UP ANY MORE

headlines.B: BUCK FITTED; A FEW STAMPS FLEW THE NEST
headlines.C: CHART WINGED, NOT BAGGED, SAYS OWL
headlines.Do-over: SITTING DUCK: BUCK'S WORKUP NEEDS A RESHOOT

subheads.S: Left ear nearer the muzzle, masked bone, no other flags: fitted, plugs and muffs, recheck set.
subheads.A: A lopsided loss with a likely cause and no other red flags can be fitted. Recheck it yearly.
subheads.B: The right call, though a few stamps strayed: mask the bone when one ear is much worse.
subheads.C: Unmasked bone hears the better cochlea, so mask it to type the poorer ear.
subheads.Do-over: One ear worse? Find out why before the call. Buck will be back at dawn.
